FICTIONAL TEST DOCUMENT. Lakshmi Rao versus Prakash Builders. The tenant occupied a commercial shop on a monthly lease for eleven years. The landlord sought eviction claiming bona fide need for personal business use. The rent controller ordered eviction, and the tenant appealed contending that no notice terminating the tenancy had been issued. The court examined whether a monthly tenancy may be terminated without notice. It held that a monthly tenancy can be terminated only after a notice of at least fifteen days expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy, and an eviction suit filed before the notice period ends is not maintainable. On the question of bona fide need, the court found that the landlord already owned two vacant shops in the same market, which undermined the claimed need. The eviction order was therefore quashed. Costs were awarded to the tenant. The court clarified that the tenant must continue paying the agreed monthly rent of eighteen thousand rupees into court until the landlord files a fresh petition, if any.
